```{python}

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import geopandas as gp
from adjustText import adjust_text

```


```{python}
data = pd.read_csv("./US County PopMigration.csv")
states_gdf = gp.read_file("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PublicaMundi/MappingAPI/master/data/geojson/us-states.json")
```

```{python}
data.info()
states_gdf.info()
```

```{python}
df = (
    pd.merge(
        data, 
        states_gdf, 
        how = "left", 
        left_on = "State", 
        right_on = "name")
    .drop(["name", "State FIPS", "County FIPS", "id", "density"], axis = 1)
    .query("County != 'State Total'")
)

df = gp.GeoDataFrame(df, geometry = "geometry")
```

# What is net migration?

Net migration is the balance of in-migrants minus out-migrants. The data do not include flows of in-migrants or out-migrants. Instead, these data include only the net balance.

```{python}
df_sum = df.groupby('State').agg({
    'Net Male Migrants': 'sum',
    'Net Female Migrants': 'sum',
    'geometry': 'first'
}).reset_index()


df_sum = gp.GeoDataFrame(df_sum, geometry = 'geometry')
```

```{python}
# 1. Filter data
# 1. Filter data
mainland = df_sum[~df_sum['State'].isin(['Alaska', 'Hawaii', 'Puerto Rico'])]

# 2. Plotting Setup
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(16, 8))

# Draw Maps
for i, col in enumerate(["Net Male Migrants", "Net Female Migrants"]):
    mainland.plot(
        column=col,
        ax=ax[i], 
        legend=True,
        cmap='RdYlGn', 
        edgecolor='black',
        legend_kwds={'label': f"{col} Population Change", 'orientation': "horizontal", 'pad': 0.05}
    )
    ax[i].axis('off')

ax[0].set_title("Male", fontsize=18)
ax[1].set_title("Female", fontsize=18)

# 3. Labeling Logic
east_coast = [
    'Massachusetts', 'Rhode Island', 'Connecticut', 'New Jersey', 
    'Delaware', 'Maryland', 'District of Columbia', 'New Hampshire', 'Vermont', 'Florida',
    'Maine', 'North Carolina', 'Virginia'
]

for idx, row in mainland.iterrows():
    # Use representative_point for the coordinates
    coords = row['geometry'].representative_point().coords[0]
    state_name = row['State']
    m_val = f"{int(row['Net Male Migrants']):,}"
    f_val = f"{int(row['Net Female Migrants']):,}"
    
    if state_name in east_coast:
        # --- MANUAL OFFSET FOR EAST COAST ---
        # We push these into the 'Atlantic' so they don't overlap
        for i, val in enumerate([m_val, f_val]):
            ax[i].annotate(
                val, 
                xy=(coords[0], coords[1]), 
                xytext=(coords[0] + 6, coords[1] + 1), # Adjusted for visibility
                fontsize=4.5,
                fontweight='bold',
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='black', lw=0.1)
            )
    elif state_name == "Montana":
        ax[0].text(coords[0], coords[1]-0.1, m_val, fontsize=5, 
                   fontweight='bold', ha='center', va='center')
        ax[1].text(coords[0], coords[1]-0.1, f_val, fontsize=5, 
                   fontweight='bold', ha='center', va='center')

    elif state_name == "Idaho":
        ax[0].text(coords[0] + 0.25, coords[1]-1, m_val, fontsize=5, 
                   fontweight='bold', ha='center', va='center')
        ax[1].text(coords[0]+ 0.25, coords[1]-1, f_val, fontsize=5, 
                   fontweight='bold', ha='center', va='center')

    else:
        # --- PERFECT CENTERING FOR EVERYTHING ELSE ---
        # By NOT using adjust_text, these will stay exactly where you put them
        ax[0].text(coords[0], coords[1], m_val, fontsize=5, 
                   fontweight='bold', ha='center', va='center')
        ax[1].text(coords[0], coords[1], f_val, fontsize=5, 
                   fontweight='bold', ha='center', va='center')

# 4. Titles and Descriptions
fig.suptitle("Net Migration by Gender and State in 2020", y=0.8, fontsize=30)

fig.text(
    0.5, 0.7, 
    "Definition: Net migration is the balance of in-migrants minus out-migrants.\n"
    "The data do not include flows of in-migrants or out-migrants. Instead, these data include only the net balance.", 
    ha='center', fontsize=12, style='italic', linespacing=1.4
)

# Crucial: Use subplots_adjust to prevent the layout engine from moving things
plt.subplots_adjust(top=0.85, bottom=0.15, wspace=0.1)

plt.savefig("./net_migrate_map.pdf", bbox_inches='tight')
plt.show()
```
